usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/maps/ip?ip={ipv4_or_ipv6} (IP as query param, no request body)
usage.outputShape: Flat top-level body: body.ip, body.country, body.country_code, body.region, body.region_code, body.city, body.postal, body.lat, body.lng, body.timezone, body.utc_offset, body.org, body.asn, body.currency
quirks: Method is GET, NOT POST — despite the registry CALL surface showing 'POST https://api.x402node.dev/maps/ip', the working call is GET with the IP as a ?ip= query parameter and no request body

Output is FLAT at top level (body.lat, body.lng, body.postal, body.org, body.asn) — this differs from the ipstack-shaped auor.io backend in prior existingUsage (which used body.country_name/body.latitude). For THIS x402node.dev endpoint read body.country, body.region, body.city, body.lat, body.lng, body.postal directly
Response includes network metadata: body.org (e.g. 'Google LLC'), body.asn (e.g. 'AS15169'), and body.currency
Observed cost was $0.005 (not the $0.001 priceAmount in the registry); price 'Varies'
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/maps/ip?ip=8.8.8.8 (substitute any IPv4/IPv6) via x402 on Base, ~$0.005 USDC per call. Pass the IP as the ?ip= query parameter — there is NO request body and do NOT use POST despite what the registry CALL line says. No auth/sign-in. Read the geolocation result directly off the top-level body: body.city, body.region, body.country, body.lat, body.lng, body.postal, plus network info body.org and body.asn. Plain synchronous response, no polling.
